item.title: The James Gunn Era is Over, Says Newly Merged Skydance: What Does This Mean for DC Fans?
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: James Gunn has only run DC Studios for a few years, and he’s already stepping down. What does that mean for the future of Skydance and the DCEU?
item.content:encoded:
Is the DCEU getting another reboot? It’s unclear.

Last month, when Paramount Skydance merged with Warner Bros. Discovery to become just Skydance, we reported that James Gunn and Peter Safran would stay on as the heads of DC Studios. That’s because Skydance’s CEO David Ellison announced that very thing: Amid shakeups in other leadership positions, the production team behind DC superhero movies would remain the same. But it looks like Skydance is walking that statement back, because Skydance just gave the filmmaking duo the boot. The circumstances around that decision are unclear, though some blame the DC Extended Universe (DCEU)’s failure to rival the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU)’s box-office numbers. Gunn also posted a statement on Instagram in response to the news, expressing some relief and saying that he prefers being a director to being a studio head. So what does this mean for the DCEU’s future? Can Skydance ever hope to compete with Disney’s MCU empire, even as the MCU’s own numbers suffer from superhero fatigue? Am I the only person watching Marvel’s “VisionQuest?” Keep reading, and we’ll talk about it.

Relive Gunn’s DC Studios lineup

Before we speculate on the future, let’s look at DC’s recent past. Gunn and Safran took over DC Studios in 2022, when the studio (formerly DC Films) was in a pretty messy state. The merger between WarnerMedia and Discovery, Inc. put David Zaslav in charge, and he made many controversial choices. One of them was shelving “Batgirl” and “Coyote vs. ACME,” two movies that were basically completed and discarded as a tax write-off. Enter James Gunn and Peter Safran. The director/producer duo found success with “The Suicide Squad” (2021) and “Peacemaker” (2022), and Warner Bros. Discovery hoped they could reboot the DCEU into something cohesive, comprehensible, and most of all, profitable. Here’s the full list of projects from the Gunn/Safran era if you’re looking to catch up:

  • “The Suicide Squad” (2021) (under DC Films)
  • “Peacemaker” (2022–2025)
  • “Creature Commandos” (2024)
  • “Superman” (2025)
  • “Supergirl” (2026)
  • “Lanterns” (2026)
  • “Clayface” (2026)

“Superman” was a critical and commercial success, but DC Studios failed to make lightning strike twice with “Supergirl” the following year. “Clayface” made less money than “Supergirl,” but was considered a success due to its lower budget. I’d say the lesson there is probably “shrink your budget and lower your expectations,” but Skydance seems to think it needs a clean slate instead. It does have a newly merged media empire to maintain, after all. Gunn and Safran are still working on “Superman: Man of Tomorrow,” which comes out next year.

The future of DC Studios and the DCEU

So who will replace Gunn and Safran as head of DC Studios? Skydance picked Jeremy Latcham, a former Marvel executive. While at Marvel, Latcham produced “Iron Man,” “The Avengers,” and “Spider-Man: Homecoming,” as well as James Gunn’s “Guardians of the Galaxy.” Ellison praised Latcham for helping “define the modern superhero movie,” clearly hoping some of that Marvel magic will transfer over to DC. Skydance isn’t canceling any in-progress DC Studios projects, so you can still look forward to “The People v. Gorilla Grodd” and Matt Reeves’ “The Batman: Part II.” DC won’t be making the “Batgirl” mistake twice. But beyond 2027’s releases, it’s unclear what Latcham’s vision for the company will be. Four months ago, before his appointment was made public, Latcham gave an interview to Christian Broadcasting News, saying he produced the early Marvel movies with his grandma as his target demographic. If his grandma liked a movie, he reasoned, it would resonate with a wide audience. That mindset seems at odds with Gunn’s vision for the DC brand, which just produced the low-budget horror title “Clayface” this year. This could mean an end to the dark-and-edgy tone that’s defined certain DC movies since Zack Snyder was in the driver’s seat. But if Ellison is trying to copy the MCU, he certainly picked a producer with the right filmography to make it happen. If this gambit doesn’t work out, DC might just have to give up on the idea of a cinematic universe — or accept that it had the perfect cinematic universe in the Arrowverse, but threw it away during the Discovery merger. No, I’m not still salty about the “Legends of Tomorrow” cliffhanger cancellation. Why do you ask?

HBO Max is currently home to most DC movies. Beginning in 2027, you’ll be able to bundle it with Paramount+.

Paramount+

Paramount+ is more Transformers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles than superheroes, so you won’t find any DC titles there. But that’s just the current state of affairs — Paramount+ is expected to bundle and eventually merge with HBO Max in the next couple of years.

Providers are offering tons of veteran and military deals

Finding the best military and veteran deals in 2026 for internet, TV, and mobile can be super overwhelming. Trust me, I know: Half of my job is hunting down exclusive service discounts. I spend my days combing through disclaimers for expiration dates and sifting through the fine print to uncover which 2026 promos actually honor your service without the hidden fees.

That’s why I wrote this page: to keep the military community and veterans up to date on the best deals providers are currently running. This page is updated monthly with fresh batches of verified offers — from free streaming subscriptions to discounted high-speed internet — so be sure to bookmark it for future reference.

What to look for in military and veteran deals

Not all military promos are created equal. Keep these tips in mind before choosing a provider to ensure you get the most value for your service.

Recurring discounts > one-time perks

A prepaid gift card is nice upfront, but a permanent rate cut saves you far more over time. Prioritize providers that discount your base plan every billing cycle rather than those that rely on flashy, short-term sign-up perks.

Military discounts vary widely in who qualifies — some cover active duty only, while others include veterans, retirees, and immediate family. Some even include other professions such as teachers, nurses, and first responders. Most companies confirm service through a site like ID.me, GovX, or SheerID, so just make sure you qualify and have your proof of service ready.

Moving flexibility

Moves and deployments happen fast, making strict contracts a costly headache. Make sure your provider of choice offers hassle-free military pause or cancellation policies with no early termination fees if your orders take you outside their coverage zone.

I think long-term discounts with no end date, like the mobile or internet deals from AT&T or Verizon Fios, are the best military offers out there. item.title: Want a Free TV for the Holidays? Verizon’s Early Black Friday Deal Has You Covered.
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Verizon launched its early Black Friday deals for Fios and 5G Home. Get two free months of service plus your choice of a free Samsung TV bundle or gift cards.
item.content:encoded:
It’s not even Thanksgiving, but Verizon is already giving away free TVs

Most internet providers — but not all, as Xfinity has shown — hold off until late November to roll out their Black Friday deals, but Verizon clearly didn’t feel like waiting around ’til Thanksgiving. As CableTV.com’s resident deals editor, keeping tabs on holiday promos is literally my job, and I’m really impressed with what Verizon is offering up this year. Depending on what Verizon internet plan you choose, new sign-ups will get two months of free service, plus your choice of a 43-inch Samsung TV and soundbar combo or up to $250 in gift cards to stores like Target or Sephora. I love it when providers let consumers choose the best perks for their own setup — not everyone needs a new TV! Still, some of these promos are locked behind higher-tier plans, so keep reading for the fine print on how to claim these early Verizon Black Friday offers, and how to suss out which deal’s the best bang for your buck.

Hook it up with the hottest in TV and internet

Stay tuned for the latest deals, show premieres, and more by signing up for our newsletter.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Which plan gets you the Samsung TV or the $250 gift card?

To get the two free months, you’ll just need to sign up for any Verizon internet plan. That’s right, none are off the table, even the lower-tier Fios 300 Mbps and Verizon’s 5G Home plans. From there, the choice comes down to which extra holiday bonus you want:

  • Totally free TV: Sign up for Fios 1 Gig or higher or 5G Home Plus or Ultimate, and Verizon will throw in a free 43-inch Samsung Neo QLED TV ($599.99 MSRP) and a Samsung B400F Soundbar ($139.99 MSRP).
  • Holiday shopping cash: Fios 5 Gig gets you a $250 reward card, while Fios 1 Gig, 2 Gig, or 5G Home Ultimate includes a $200 reward card. You can use your gift card at one of nine brands of your choice, including Target, Sephora, Macy’s, or Nordstrom.

Two months is already a solid breather for your Wi-Fi budget during the holiday season. The additional perk you choose depends on what’s best for your family. Sure, the $740 total value of the Samsung bundle easily beats the highest gift card amount, but if you already have a sick TV setup, that may just go to waste. $200+ in gift cards can be a real lifesaver this holiday shopping season, helping offset inflation woes one gift at a time.Looking for more holiday discounts? See the latest ways to save in our guide to Verizon deals and promotions, or browse our main hub for the best Black Friday deals across every major internet, TV, and streaming provider.

item.title: You Can Watch About 475 NBA G League Games for Free This Season — Here’s How
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: The NBA made it easier for fans of up-and-coming players to watch G League games. Find out where to watch them and what platforms you’ll need.
item.content:encoded:
Free G League games coming to NBA app and website

The NBA just made it easier to watch the G League. Starting in the 2026–2027 season, the NBA app and NBA.com will stream G League games that aren’t broadcast on national networks. Fans can watch about 475 games for free, without needing NBA League Pass or an NBA ID login. These specific NBA G League games will still be available locally, per the league.

Want more TV sports coverage?

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest event-viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Where to watch other NBA G League games

For games that aren’t available for free on the league’s app or website, fans can tune in through a variety of national broadcast partners. The list includes Amazon Prime Video, ESPN, NBA TV, Roku, and Samsung TV Plus. ESPN recently announced that more than 150 NBA G League games will air on ESPN+, ESPNU, and ESPNews.

CableTV.com verdict: Free G League games should be the default viewing situation

The NBA is wildly popular, with games available across a wide mix of local and national TV networks and streaming services. But its developmental arm, the G League, is, unsurprisingly, less well known. The news that the NBA is making so many G League games free via its website and app feels appropriate. In fact, the league could — and should — just make its entire slate of G League games free to watch. The NBA makes enough money with its 30 teams. The current media deal alone is reportedly worth $76 billion over 11 years. And that’s not to mention other types of revenue like ticket sales, concessions, merchandise, and more. So let’s just rip the band-aid off and make every G League game free. If it all lives on the NBA app and website, fine. It doesn’t need to be more complicated than that. It would be a way to truly grow the game of basketball even further and attract new fans.

item.title: “If You Think It Was Made Up, It Probably Was.” “MP3” Cast Interview Reveals a Behind-the-Scenes Look at Dropout’s Musical Comedy
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: We sat down with the cast of Dropout’s new show, “MP3,” including Aparna Nancherla, Skye Townsend, and Paul F. Tompkins.
item.content:encoded:
Dropout’s new show brings music videos back, back again

When the YouTube channel CollegeHumor became the streaming service Dropout, it left sketch comedy behind in favor of improv and game shows. But the platform is returning to its roots this week with the premiere of its new scripted comedy, “MP3.” “MP3” is a show about a show — specifically, an MTV-era, music-video-compilation variety show. Hosted by former heartthrob Dane Cartel (Jeremy Culhane), “MP3” highlights comedy songs written by Jessica McKenna and Zach Reino and sung by fictional pop stars.
The trailer above gives a pretty good overview of what you can expect. The show premiered today, November 4, at 7 p.m. ET, which means you can go and stream the first episode on Dropout right now. The pilot, “Mid-Size Courtside Beverages,” features songs performed by comedians Jess McKenna, Lily Du, Anna Garcia, Jacob Wysocki, and Lou Wilson. Culhane is joined by Aparna Nancherla, Skye Townsend, and Paul F. Tompkins, who also play characters on the fictional show’s set. I sat down with the three of them last week to learn more about the process of filming “MP3.” Keep reading to find out what they had to say! Or check out the full video on our YouTube channel.

An interview with Aparna Nancherla, Skye Townsend, and Paul F. Tompkins

Aparna Nancherla is a comedian and voice actor who produced a stand-up special with Dropout called “Hopeful Potato.” In “MP3,” she plays Chia, one of the two new co-hosts brought onto the show to cramp Dane Cartel’s style. Skye Townsend is an actress, singer, and TV host, and this is her first Dropout project. In “MP3,” she plays Dr. Muse-Tina, Dane’s other wacky co-host. Paul F. Tompkins is a comedian, actor, and podcaster who’s appeared in many Dropout projects including “Very Important People,” “Crowd Control,” and “Make Some Noise. In “MP3,” he plays Thomas Cartel, Dane’s father and the producer of the fictional variety show.

How does the process of filming “MP3” compare to the process of filming Dropout’s improv shows versus this new scripted one?

Paul F. Tompkins: Oh wow, it’s different in a lot of ways because the other shows, there’s not really an audience, you know? Like, “Make Some Noise” or “Game Changer” are things that are participated in, “Dirty Laundry,” it’s like, sometimes the crew will be laughing, sometimes they don’t laugh, you know, it depends on what the vibe is for that particular show. So to be on a show with even a fake audience there, that is responding and giving audience energy and everything, that absolutely changes the dynamic already. Even though you have to remember, like, they’re not a real audience. They’re paid to be here. They’re reacting the way they’re told to react. But it’s also the idea of following a story, as opposed to doing short bursts of comedy, that is so much fun. I’ve always been a fan of narrative-improv, narrative-sketch, like things that are funny, that are longer than sketch-length, but they’re not really a sitcom, you know what I mean? Like, I remember when I was a kid, the earliest example of that was there was an episode of “Monty Python” where they did one story through the whole episode. They never did it again until they started doing the movies, and it was so exciting! For some reason it was so exciting to me as a kid, it was like, “Oh my god, they can do that too!” So to do something like this, “MP3,” which has a bunch of, you know, sort of sketch-y elements to it, but there is a story that’s unfolding in each episode, was so much fun. Cause you get to do both, you know? You get to be silly, but also you get to be acting certain moments and furthering a narrative is really a blast.

Was any of “MP3” improv or was it all truly scripted?

Aparna Nancherla: Oh my gosh, it was so much improv. They gave us a bare-bones skeleton script and then they were like, “Play! Go off the rails, do whatever you want, we want you to really have ownership over these characters, help build this world with us.” If you think it was made up, it probably was. Skye Townsend: If it sounded like, “Who approved this?” It was probably improv, yeah. It was pretty much 50/50. We were given guidelines, but then it’d be stuff like, “the two hosts discuss their family history.” And then from that, we went into our stories and then Paul would interrupt and be like, “We’re filming!” And then we’d get back to it. And so tons of it is improv. Of course, we haven’t seen it yet, so we don’t know what was kept in. But I think to keep the flow of the show, it requires improv because there were these wide-open gaps where we filled in the blanks for these characters. And so it allowed us all to come up with all of these absurd backgrounds, and life history, and family situations, because there was just so much room to improvise. So yeah, a lot of improv.

If you think it was made up, it probably was.

Aparna Nancherla

So you had a lot of influence over your characters. Did you have a lot of influence over your costume choices as well?

Tompkins: 100%. They gave us so much room… I don’t know if they said no to anything. It was just like, “If you want this, absolutely.” And that’s such a gift, you know? Because a big part of the fun of creating characters, like if I do a live character on stage, is putting together the costume and the look of what this person would look like in real life, it’s such a fun sort of puzzle that you’re putting together. And then to have somebody else be in charge of the budget is great. And they’re not saying no? I don’t have to go to Hollywood Toys & Costumes to buy this, they will source this thing for me, and it will be better than the thing I would have bought on my own. Townsend: Yeah, they asked us to bring in a lot of pieces. They were like, “Do you have anything that would work for the character? Bring it in!” And of course we all did but we weren’t in each other’s fittings, obviously, and so, you know, I would see Paul the next day and I’d be like, “That shirt is hilarious.” And he’s like, “It’s mine!” Tompkins: My approach was to bring in things that I would wear, but I would not wear them together. Townsend: Stuff was ours, like my jumper, the blue jumper, my green pants, my green blazer with cutout sides, that was all my stuff. But yeah, it was really fun, I think in creating these characters, we got so much freedom and so when I came in… Paul said earlier, he was like, “You were just trying anything and they said yes to everything!” It was like neverending, I’m like, “What about bangs? What about braces? What about…” You know, and they approved everything, and so when it all came together, we didn’t know what it was gonna look like until that day. And so it was so much fun as like, the wig got cut, the braces popped in, the brows were gone, I was like “Oh my god, she’s coming to life,” it was like Frankenstein! So that was really, really fun, and as we started to figure out, like, “That’s your wardrobe, oh those are your glasses, that’s not your natural hair…” Tompkins: We would ask each other the question over and over, “Is that yours or did wardrobe…?” The answer was always the same, but we kept asking the question. Townsend: Just all the characters are so different that it just gave us this amazing baseline for improvising. Because it was like, you already know, if they had to react to the same thing they would all react differently, because they’re such fleshed out, unique characters. And so it was so easy to improvise with each other because no one felt similar in any way.

I would see Paul the next day and I'd be like, "That shirt is hilarious." And he's like, "It's mine!"

Skye Townsend

As someone with a background in music, is it sort of weird interviewing fake musicians? What’s that like, to be a musician entering a “fake” music space?

Townsend: Oh man! It’s super fun. I used to be a red carpet host. Well I’ve had many little lives, you know? You hustle it out until something sticks. And so, when I was a teenager, I was a singer and I worked at a label, and then I was like, “This isn’t for me!” And now I’m a recording artist, and now I’m a host, and so being in this world… It’s so much fun because I think they did such a great job of the music sounding good. There’s nothing I can’t stand more than bad comedy music where it’s purposefully really bad, and it’s just like, “Just do it well, it’s alright!” And so the fact that they did it well is such a treat because you’re not going to listen to the song and be cringing, melodically you’re enjoying yourself. And that really makes the show so much better. I had so much fun because I just really love music. I think seeing how well the creators of this show incorporated all of these genres, like it wasn’t even just pop records, or rock, they had emo bands. I mean, they did a really great job of just like, crossing every single genre and making sure that everybody has something that they’ll enjoy on this show. I truly was blown away not only when I heard the concept of the show, but when I saw how it was run, I was like, “They thought through everything.” Tompkins: Yeah. I gotta stress how amazing Jessica McKenna and Zach Reino are. I mean, they’re amazing artists in themselves, and then they obviously care about this stuff. Music is such a huge part of who they are. And so, going into these different genres and also creating the characters of who would sing these songs… They got the best people to embody these songs and the production on them is so great. It’s like one of those things where the harder you try to make it feel real, the funnier it’s gonna be. The more you try to make it sound like it’s sincere, the more hilarious it ends up being. And they did such a wonderful job.

Are the songs fully completed before you film the show?

Nancherla: Yeah, yeah. I think we watched all the videos on our own before we shot anything, but it was kind of fun to get to see these studio audiences watch them in real time. And just like, you know, pan out. The songs are earworms. They get in your ear, and they’re, like, genuinely fun songs.

It's like one of those things where the harder you try to make it feel real, the funnier it's gonna be. The more you try to make it sound like it's sincere, the more hilarious it ends up being.

Paul F. Tompkins

Any favorites among the songs?

Tompkins: Man, it’s so many great people, look out for Lou Wilson and Rashawn Scott. And there’s a boy band that includes Angela Giarratana, and they’re all amazing. Nancherla: Yeah. They’re all so different, too. They’re all so different, it’s hard to pick a favorite because the genres are all unique.

The “MP3” cast’s favorite music videos

I couldn’t let the interview end without asking the cast for their favorite real-world music videos from the MTV era. Here are some of their picks, embedded here for your listening pleasure!

Paul F. Tompkins: “Around the World” by Daft Punk

Tompkins on “Around the World”: It’s all these characters just going around. I’ve watched that video a million times. Not even high!

Aparna Nancherla: “Shiny Happy People” by R.E.M., “Last Resort” by Papa Roach

Nancherla on “Last Resort”: It’s fun cause it’s these people just like, being angry on camera. They’re all just angry lipsyncing this song. And I dunno, it really did it for my teenage self.

Skye Townsend: “Bootylicious” by Destiny’s Child, “Bring Me To Life” by Evanescence

Townsend on “Bring Me To Life”: She was just a gorgeous vampire. Oh, love it. So good!

Where to watch “MP3”

Dropout

Dropout is a comedy streaming service brought to you by the folks who made CollegeHumor so popular in the Before Times. It’s the exclusive home of “Dimension 20,” “Game Changer,” “Very Important People,” and more.

item.title: Optimum Prepares to File for Bankruptcy — What It Means for Customers
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: The national ISP Optimum will file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy this fall, but what does that mean for customers?
item.content:encoded:
Optimum’s creditors want their money back

As reported earlier this week, New York-based internet service provider Optimum is expected to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy by the end of 2026. In a nutshell, creditors are forcing a reorganization of Optimum because of roughly $26 billion of debt. The ISP has struggled to maintain its footing in a competitive marketplace, as it has lost more than 500,000 residential customers since 2022 and its share price is averaging less than $1.00 in recent months. But what does that mean for existing Optimum customers and folks currently looking for service in Optimum areas? Read on to find out.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Has rapid expansion benefited Optimum customers?

Leveraging debt, Optimum bought up Suddenlink and Cablevision roughly 10 years ago to increase its footprint and profits. The potential profits have taken a back seat to debt repayment, and the cable giant has recently streamlined its cable TV service and increased its internet speeds to remain competitive in a market led by fiber and 5G providers. The same goes for starting prices. Optimum home internet pricing remained relatively flat from 2020–2025, as CableTV.com previously reported, standing out in an inflation-addled economy. Optimum service can sound competitive on paper, but our annual customer satisfaction survey results tell a very different story. Optimum customers came in last place in our 2026 cable TV survey, and Optimum internet service placed in the lowest quartile of overall customer satisfaction, too. So, although advertised internet speeds rose and internet pricing beat inflation, it appears that the debt from footprint expansion has done little to improve customer experience and worried its creditors in the process.

Will Optimum service continue to operate as usual?

Optimum is not going out of business, but the ownership structure is expected to change, which could lead to radical restructuring. Although we don’t know all of the details of the restructuring, recent history demonstrates that it’s likely Optimum will continue to deliver service at similar levels. For example, DISH filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy this summer, and DISH satellite customers have enjoyed uninterrupted service though the summer and into the fall. That said, DISH raised prices by $5 per month shortly thereafter in September 2026. Considering Optimum’s current debt load and below-market internet pricing, we think it’s likely Optimum will raise its prices again after filing for bankruptcy to help pay down more debt. We’ll keep monitoring the situation, so stay tuned!

In this article

Optimum

Although we don’t see Optimum service changing drastically after its bankruptcy filing, and its first-year internet pricing is very competitive, we say go with another provider because of Optimum’s low customer satisfaction and meh TV plans.

DISH Network

Bankruptcy is just one indicator that DISH has been on the decline for the past three or four years. We say go with DIRECTV if you’re looking for traditional satellite service or if you want the look and feel of cable in a streaming service.
